newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission energy tax plans face delay.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission energy tax plans face delay.

text.p: The European Commission does not expect to finalise its plans for a directive on taxation of energy products at a meeting on Wednesday, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said on Tuesday.

"The Commission will begin with a discussion on the political advisability of taking intitiatives in this field. Personally, I am not expecting a final decision," he said in reference to scheduled Commission talks on the tax proposals.
Commission plans to raise taxes on petrol and diesel fuel have been criticised by industry as an attempt to introduce by the back door a tax on the EU's carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions.
The planned proposal would increase EU-wide minimum excise duties on motor and heating fuels.
If approved, proposals would also impose a minimum tax on electricity, natural gas and coal which are not currently covered by EU rules.
But for most products the minimum levels would be below the actual rates currently levied in the 15-nation bloc.

Like an old plan to create a European tax on CO2 emissions, the new proposal has run into fierce opposition from the European oil industry as well as major energy-intensive sectors such as the steel, cement and chemical industries.
A second Commission official, who asked not to be named, said a majority of the 20 Commissioners opposed adoption of the plan for the moment.
"They do not object to the idea as such but they are questioning whether it should be proposed now," the official told Reuters.

"If you propose something like that now, when everybody is striving to respect the EMU (economic and monetary union) criteria, you have to ask whether it is politically opportune to do so," the official said.
